Hello, 

I'm currently preparing a Shiny presentation/training for novice R and ignorant html/Javascript participants. At the stage of the slide below, the participants have launched their first Shiny app on their computer. Thus it is time to consider the question 'What does runApp do?'. Please could you say me whether the sentence 'Javascript handles the connection between R and the interface'  is correct ? (and any other remark about this slide is welcomed).

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: help for a slide (how does shiny work ?)
parts: Yes, that's fair to say. In particular there is one file called shiny.js that ships with the package and gets served to the browser; it initiates the connection from the browser (client) to R (server), using a WebSocket, and also handles all subsequent communication between the client and server.

messages.subject: Re: help for a slide (how does shiny work ?)
parts:
A preliminary version: http://stla.github.io/ShinyPresentationI_v0. This is a 2 hour presenttation-training. 

The slide deck contains some shiny apps (actually, one shiny app separated in several slides) but this functionality is not available with the above link. To view the slide deck locally on your computer :

 - download the repo https://github.com/stla/ShinyPresentationI_v0

 - install the required packages :
require(devtools)
install_github(c('slidify', 'slidifyLibraries'), 'ramnathv', ref = 'dev')
install_github('rCharts', 'ramnathv')

 - set the downloaded repo as the working directory and run the slide deck :
library(slidify)
runDeck()
 
Any suggestion for improvement is welcomed.
